target_customer: Pharmaceutical and clinical partners; originally amputees and prosthetics makers
problem: Prosthetics lacked a standard nerve interface; later the goal broadened to reading and writing nerve signals for medicine.
business_model: Partnerships with pharma and clinical groups for neural digital therapies, grants

founders.name: Emil Hewage
founders.background_notes: Described as a computational neuroscientist in TechCrunch Dec 2018.

founders.name: Oliver Armitage
founders.background_notes: Described as a bioengineer in TechCrunch Dec 2018.

technical_complexity.rationale: Neural interfaces that read and write nerve signals combine hardware, signal processing and clinical validation, which is research grade and regulated.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated nerve data and clinical programs could compound, but this was early and unproven at founding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; the company remains independent.

market_need_then: Prosthetic users and clinicians wanted direct nerve control; the company claimed its interface could cut limb costs about 60 percent, which is its own claim.

identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific; code for the nervous system framing

rebrands.why: Not stated; scope broadened beyond prosthetics. Date inferred from the 2018 TechCrunch article already using BIOS

branding.community_and_virality: Awards listed on its site include Europas Top Healthcare Startup in Europe 2019 and Wired Health EY Startup of the Year 2021.

brand_strength.rationale: Award and trade press visibility, but a short generic name shared with many companies.

pivots.to: AI driven neural interface and neural digital therapies
pivots.why: Longer term goal stated in TechCrunch Dec 2018 was reading and writing nerve signals for chronic conditions

outcome_analysis: BIOS started as a Cambridge prosthetics interface startup, renamed and widened into AI based neural medicine, raised a 4.5M seed in December 2018 and an undisclosed round in June 2023, and is running clinical study work with partners. It is still pre commercial and capital needs are large relative to the funding publicly seen.
notes: The 2023 round was not disclosed in the press release; CB Insights lists 20M Series A and 26.2M total over 11 rounds, unverified so not recorded. Aggregators give totals of 26M to 47M. The 2023 round source was seen only as a search result, not opened. Competitor list empty: no 2016 to 2017 dated source found. Education and prior employers not found. Founding year conflicts (2015 vs Cambridge graduation July 2016).
